epics.name: Launch-1 billing baseline & hardening
epics.goal: Phase 12 as built (webhook-only writer, gates, portal, copy) kept green, plus the two things it never proved: a real failed renewal and a lapse, and a boot-time assertion of the live account's fee/tax state before live keys go in.

epics.name: Catalog & entitlements engine (Phase 18)
epics.goal: Prices, limits and feature keys live in MySQL and resolve from grants ("highest wins"); code asks has(feature)/limit(key), never "is Pro"; the webhook stays the only writer of subscription grants; /pricing and the extension read the same catalog.

epics.name: Margin guard & unit economics
epics.goal: One MarginCalculator with Stripe's real fee schedule (card, Billing 0.7 %, optional Managed Payments 3.5 %, tax, international blend, disputes) guards every publish, promo, student and regional price, and a nightly realised-margin report closes the loop against the 80 % / 20 % floors.

epics.name: Checkout, upgrade sheet & plan switching
epics.goal: Any catalog price (Pro, Autopilot, monthly or 3-month) buyable in one honest flow: the price-with-date line on every CTA, consent recorded, Link/Apple/Google Pay, return to where you were, Pro↔Autopilot switching in-app with a prorated preview.

epics.name: Subscription lifecycle: invoices, renewals, dunning, lapse
epics.goal: Webhook v2 mirrors invoices and period start, writes grants, reminds before every renewal, runs a three-step dunning cadence with a one-tap card update, and turns a lapse into a "nothing lost" moment with a reactivate path.

epics.name: Cancel & win-back, honestly
epics.goal: Cancel in two taps inside the app with a cancellation number, a confirmation email and an undo until period end; reasons asked after, never before; no retention gates; one consented win-back email after lapse. The #1 one-star theme of every competitor, done right (G29).

epics.name: Tax, invoices & legal compliance
epics.goal: A recorded tax mode for the live Stripe account (Managed Payments vs Stripe Tax vs none) that the margin guard knows about, invoices and receipts in-app, consent records and EU withdrawal handling, financial records that survive account deletion pseudonymised.

epics.name: Discounts, promos, students & regional pricing
epics.goal: Discounts are products with their own budgets, not coupons that breach the floor: a verified Pro Student plan, local-currency display at launch and guarded regional Pro Lite rows later, governed promo codes, referral credits as grants, explicit stacking rules (G34, G37).

epics.name: AI budget economics & top-ups
epics.goal: The AI budget window follows the real billing period from the invoice mirror, quarterly plans pool one budget, usage rides on /api/billing/me, and a guard-checked one-time top-up waits for the cap-hit data that decides whether it should exist.

epics.name: Org & services billing engine hooks
epics.goal: One Stripe seam and one webhook router for three scopes (user, org, service order): one-time checkout and send-invoice invoices, item quantity ops, refunds and a payout-ledger hook — the engine the org and services designs (O4.*, O9.*) plug into.

epics.name: Billing ops, reconciliation & observability
epics.goal: Nightly Stripe-vs-mirror reconciliation that alerts and never writes money, failed-event alerts and an audited replay tool, billing metrics (MRR by product, churn, cap-hit, conversion), a FakeStripeGateway scenario harness in CI, and billing events in the product analytics pipeline.

epics.name: Plan surfaces across extension & mobile
epics.goal: The extension gates on features not plan names and deep-links every upgrade to the web with a return path; purchases start on the web only (no in-extension or in-app purchase); billing notices flow through the one notification engine.
